newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: U.N. envoy expected in S.Africa to set Zaire summit.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy expected in S.Africa to set Zaire summit.

text.p: U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun will return to South Africa on Thursday to settle a date and a venue for direct talks between the battling parties in Zaire, South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said.
Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko and rebel leader Laurent Kabila had both reaffirmed their commitment to a negotiated peace, he said, adding:
"The only issue now outstanding is that we need to determine the time and the place where the meeting should take place."

Pahad said Sahnoun, who also represents the Organisation of African Unity in his efforts to end the Zairean civil war, had visited Angola and Namibia and was expected back in South Africa on Thursday evening.
"We will have consultations with him and other interested role players to finally determine the time and the venue of this very important summit," Pahad said.
South African President Nelson Mandela has formally invited Mobutu to meet Kabila in South Africa, but officials have said the ailing Zairean president is too ill to travel that far.
Mobutu's son and spokesman, Nzanga Mobutu, said on Wednesday his father was still prepared to meet Kabila, but the question remained where.

The president, who had prostate cancer surgery last August, wants the talks held in the Congolese capital Brazzaville -- just across the river from Kinshasa. Kabila has proposed Lubumbashi, Zaire's second city, which is under his control.
Nzanga said his father had declined to travel to South Africa, on health grounds, and Kabila had rejected Brazzaville.

Despite Kabila's stated willingness to meet Mobutu, his rebel forces, who control over half of the Central African country after six months of fighting, have continued to march on Kinshasa, which he has identified as their final major target.
